papers.summary: We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones. Hence we obtain a completeness theorem for $\pm$-preclones: a set of $\pm$-operations generates all $\pm$-operations if and only if it contains an operation that fails to preserve each of the nine defining $\pm$-relations of the maximal $\pm$-preclones. Next we classify the twenty minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones (atoms of the lattice), each described via a generating $\pm$-operation. We also investigate self-dual $\pm$-preclones, characterizing the eight maximal and nine minimal self-dual $\pm$-preclones and proving a corresponding completeness theorem. Additionally, we include the result, due to Vojtěch David, that the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ is uncountable, in contrast with the countability of the classical Post lattice of Boolean clones. This is established by embedding an uncountable poset of clonoids into ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$. Finally, we study preimage classes of classical Boolean clones within ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$, providing complete descriptions for the unary case and for several non-unary minimal clones. We also prove a Baker--Pixley type theorem for $\pm$-preclones containing the majority operation, showing that such $\pm$-preclones are determined by their binary $\pm$-relations.
papers.title: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones

papers.summary: We characterize the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces for exponents satisfying $1<p_-\le p_+<\infty$. We show that $M$ is bounded on $L^{p(\cdot)}_w$ if and only if the pair $(p(\cdot),w)$ satisfies a variable Muckenhoupt condition and there exists $h\in L^1$ such that $w^{-1}h^{1/p(\cdot)}$ and $wh^{1/p'(\cdot)}$ belong to $A_1$. This characterization is new even in the unweighted setting. To prove sufficiency, we use sparse domination together with a local modular averaging estimate whose error terms are summable over sparse families to $\|h\|_{L^1}$. Conversely, assuming $M$ is bounded, we construct $h$ using a simultaneous Rubio de Francia algorithm. To motivate this new characterization, we show that the strong Muckenhoupt condition, which characterizes the boundedness of $M$ in the unweighted case by a theorem of Diening, is not sufficient in the weighted setting. As applications, we give short proofs and extensions of known sufficient conditions.
papers.title: An $A_1$ characterization of the boundedness of the maximal function on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces

papers.summary: We prove unconditionally that the first-order theory of Presburger arithmetic expanded by a predicate for the primes is undecidable. Bateman, Jockusch and Woods proved this in 1993 assuming Dickson's conjecture. We use the counter-machine framework of Karimov, Nieuwveld and Ouaknine and their idea of using `arbitrary permutations', and the number-theoretic input comes from Hildebrand and Maier's 1988 proof that the limit points of $k$ consecutive normalised prime gaps have positive measure. We use a discrete version, which they obtain before limits are taken. The key lemma is that although Hildebrand and Maier's result does not seem to give arbitrary permutations of consecutive prime gaps, it gives arbitrary permutations for the differences $p_i - q_i$ for two finite blocks of consecutive primes $p_0 < \cdots < p_k$ and $q_0 < \cdots < q_k$. Moreover, with the same key lemma, we show that Presburger arithmetic expanded with the function that maps $n$ to the $n$th prime defines multiplication.
papers.title: On Presburger Arithmetic Expanded with Prime Numbers

papers.summary: Tensor train (TT) methods enable high-resolution computational mechanics simulations by exploiting low-rank structure in discretized fields and operators. While the superfast Fourier transform (SFFT) has enabled efficient TT-based spectral solvers for periodic problems, corresponding representations for non-periodic boundary conditions remain underexplored. We introduce the superfast cosine and sine transforms (SFCT and SFST), extending the TT spectral framework to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. Building on a quantum-circuit construction of the discrete cosine and sine transforms, we derive both transforms from a shared TT operator representation and prove that their TT ranks are bounded by $6r_S$, independently of the discretization order, where $r_S$ is the rank of the SFFT at the prescribed accuracy. The measured ranks plateau near 32 for grid sizes up to $2^{26}$ points. For Rayleigh-Bénard convection, spectral pressure projection achieves up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve relative to a preconditioned physical-space TT solver while maintaining comparable accuracy. Three-dimensional computational homogenization achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold reduction in memory consumption compared with the existing TT-based approach. The results establish an efficient TT framework for spectral PDE solvers with non-periodic boundary conditions.
papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions

papers.summary: In this work, we extend the Intrinsic Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume method for the Intrinsic Shallow Water Equations (ISWE) to account for localized topographic discontinuities that influence flow patterns. The ISWE formulation is modified to incorporate these bottom perturbations without altering the global structure of the system. The numerical discretization is based on a Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume scheme within an intrinsic geometric framework and consists of a Lagrangian evolution step followed by an Eulerian remapping onto a fixed reference grid. The combination of the intrinsic nature of the ISWE formulation and the dual Lagrangian-Eulerian structure of the proposed discretization yields a numerical method that naturally satisfies the three key properties essential for stability, accuracy, and robustness: well-balancing for preservation of the lake-at-rest equilibrium over irregular bathymetry; wetting-and-drying, enabling robust tracking of moving fluid boundaries; and hyperbolicity guaranteeing consistency with the system wave propagation and stability constraints. Numerical experiments on curved two-dimensional surfaces with localized bottom discontinuities demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the method, including accurate long-time velocity computations in near-dry conditions and transitions between wet and dry states.
papers.title: A robust Lagrangian-Eulerian Finite Volume scheme for intrinsic shallow water equations with wetting-and-drying transitions on locally discontinuous beds

papers.summary: Stochastic Galerkin methods reformulate a differential equation with uncertain parameters as a deterministic surrogate system by writing the solution as a series of polynomial basis functionals and projecting onto the parameter space. Given correlated Gaussian parameters, Rahman (2017) established solution convergence when the basis functionals are multivariate Hermite polynomials (MHPs), which is the setting considered here. Each term of the original equation contributes coefficients to the surrogate system, which we call the $N$th moments, that are expectations of products of the basis polynomials. Since the parameters are dependent, the $N$th moments do not factor into one-dimensional expectations via tensorization as they do in the independent case; consequently, their values are typically determined numerically at a nontrivial and compounding cost. Namely, the number of $N$th moments that emerge grows combinatorially with parameter dimension and truncation order. In this paper, we first relate MHPs and slowly growing functions --- which are smooth functions whose derivatives of all orders grow at most polynomially --- in correlated Gaussian parameters. In doing so, we derive an expression for the $N$th moment of an MHPs in terms of $(N-1)$th moments that can be evaluated exactly, along with sufficient conditions for the $N$th moment to vanish. Numerical examples illustrate the benefit of evaluating such moments directly without numerical approximation and confirm that formula-predicted values match sampling-based estimates.
papers.title: Higher-Order Moments of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials

papers.summary: CholeskyQR is an orthogonalization algorithm particularly well suited to modern computing architectures, but it may fail to produce numerically orthonormal columns when applied to ill-conditioned matrices. A customary solution is to first reduce the condition number of the input matrix by means of a preconditioner, and then apply CholeskyQR to the preconditioned matrix. We propose three mixed-precision techniques for constructing such preconditioners: mpSCQR, based on a shifted Cholesky factorization; mpEVDQR, based on the eigendecomposition; and mpLUCQR, based on a pivoted LU factorization. We prove bounds on the condition number of the matrix after mpSCQR, mpLUCQR, or a shifted variant of mpEVDQR has been applied. Our experiments compare the proposed preconditioners with existing deterministic and randomized alternatives. The results suggest that mpEVDQR and mpLUCQR can be substantially faster than traditional shiftedCholeskyQR, with mpLUCQR attaining performance comparable to that of the most efficient randomized preconditioners.
papers.title: Three mixed-precision preconditioners for CholeskyQR

papers.summary: Kinematic wave models, the simplest surface flow models, route overland flow by gravity alone and there is no pressure or inertial term to redistribute flow when the resulting velocities misroute it. Computed from piecewise-linear elevation data, this velocity jumps across the edges of the mesh: two neighboring cells can push water into each other, and the scheme can hold water in ponds that the terrain does not contain, or concentrate it where the data do not. We formulate the model intrinsically on the bed surface, with the depth normal to the bed as unknown, and obtain a single-valued edge velocity, in the unique edge frame of the intrinsic geometry, by correcting the raw cell field with the star-based conservative flux of Larson and Niklasson. Because the field is derived from data rather than from a Galerkin solution, the local problems are solvable only with a compatible load, the weak discrete divergence of the field being corrected, which for the slope is a discrete mean curvature of the terrain. With a Neumann boundary, every element is conservative, and the corrected field reproduces the cell average of the nodal divergence of the raw field, plus the divergence resolved inside the curved cells. Since any single-valued flux conserves mass, the correction is about consistency and robustness: the steady state of the upwind scheme solves an M-matrix system exactly when every cell drains to an outlet, and spurious ponds are closed classes of a transfer directed graph, computable before any simulation. Four rainfall tests, from a plane to a real catchment, are designed to verify the difference in storage and timing between the intrinsic and the classical form, the effect of the mesh on the consistency of the edge velocity, the robustness at a degenerate stationary point, and the application to terrain data.
papers.title: An intrinsic kinematic wave model with conservative fluxes for overland flow on curved terrain

papers.summary: We construct a two-sided noetherian ring $A$ which has injective dimension $1$ as a left module over itself and infinite injective dimension as a right module over itself. This shows that Gorenstein symmetry can fail for two-sided noetherian rings. It is further shown that there is such an example over any field of characteristic different than $2$, that it has a dualizing complex, and that its derived category of right modules does not satisfy injective-generation in the sense of Rickard-Keller.
papers.title: Gorenstein symmetry can fail for noetherian rings

papers.summary: Synthetic topology encompasses various alternatives to the classical definition of a topological space by Hausdorff. In particular, Abstract Stone Duality (ASD) develops the theory of locally compact spaces directly from logic. This study introduces a semi-formal theory of synthetic topology using a first-order version of the intuitionistic modal logic iS4, inspired by a nominalist, dynamic interpretation of the specialization order. The remarkable similarities to ASD include a constructive interpretation of the open-closed duality, overtness of the line, compactness of the unit interval and the nuclei that define closed and open subspaces.
papers.title: An approach to topology via lattices of names

papers.summary: We study strong $r$-variation estimates for the free Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq3$. Combining fractal and weighted restriction estimates with mixed space--time estimates, we determine the sharp Sobolev regularity, up to endpoints, in several ranges of the spatial exponent $p$ and the variation exponent $r$. In particular, our results give a sharp $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ variational extension of the Schrödinger maximal estimate of Du and Zhang [\emph{Ann. of Math.}, \textbf{189}, 837--861 (2019)].
papers.title: Sharp variational estimates for Schrödinger equation in higher dimensions

papers.summary: We form a hexagonal prism from two six-cycles and iterate a doubling construction with a fixed positive integer edge multiplicity, producing a family of indefinite Kac--Moody algebras. The prism's spectrum determines the exact corank of every algebra in the family. Along each nonvanishing parity class, the corank grows exponentially, while its ratio to the matrix size tends to zero. For the twelve-node algebra we identify the two central directions, describe the first two graded levels, and characterize the integral central charges of its unitary highest-weight modules.
papers.title: A Systematic Construction of High-Corank Kac--Moody Algebras

papers.summary: We prove that every quasicircle $Γ\subset\mathbb{C}$ admits an optimal admissible polynomial mesh for univariate complex polynomials. More precisely, if $E$ denotes the closed Jordan domain bounded by $Γ$, then for every $Λ>1$ there are finite sets $A_n\subsetΓ$ with $\mathrm{card}(A_n)=O(n)$ and $\|p\|_E=\|p\|_Γ\leqΛ\|p\|_{A_n}$ for every $p\in\mathcal{P}_n(\mathbb{C})$. The nodes may be chosen as images of equally spaced points of the unit circle under the inverse exterior conformal map, equivalently as equal-mass points for harmonic measure at infinity. The proof combines the classical conformal level-curve scale with a discrete norming principle. If $ρ_n(z)$ denotes the distance from a boundary point to the exterior level curve $|Φ|=1+1/n$, Bernstein--Walsh and Cauchy's formula show that any sufficiently fine $ρ_n$-net is norming. A scale-comparison property then turns $O(n)$ equally spaced angular samples into such a net. Quasicircles satisfy this property by quasisymmetry. The argument requires no smoothness or rectifiability and applies in particular to the classical von Koch snowflake.
papers.title: Optimal polynomial meshes on quasicircles via conformal scale comparison

papers.summary: We consider the heat-diffusion semigroup related to expansions with respect to an orthogonal system emerging by taking arbitrary finite tensor products of classical Hermite, Laguerre and Jacobi polynomials. Our main result is the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for the associated maximal operator. This implies pointwise almost everywhere boundary convergence of the semigroup to initial values for all initial conditions that are integrable against the orthogonality measure.
papers.title: On the maximal operator of the hybrid Hermite-Laguerre-Jacobi semigroup

papers.summary: Let $R$ be a Gorenstein ring with left and right self-injective dimensions $n$. We prove that the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $_RR$ has an essential socle. It answers an open question of Iwanaga and Sato. As a consequence, we get that for any left $R$-module $M$ with injective dimension $n$, the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $M$ also has an essential socle.
papers.title: The socle of the last term in a minimal injective resolution II

papers.summary: We study Hardy and BMO spaces associated with the Laplacian with drift. We define an atomic Hardy space $H^1$ whose atoms satisfy cancellation against constants and linear functions in directions perpendicular to the drift. We prove the John--Nirenberg inequality, Hardy--BMO duality, equivalence of finite and infinite atomic norms, and interpolation theorems. We show that the Riesz transforms and their adjoints are bounded from $H^1$ to $L^1$ and from $L^\infty$ to BMO. Moreover, we prove that the cancellation conditions are optimal, but the Riesz transforms do not characterize $H^1$. We also characterize the $L^p$ boundedness of their commutators, $1<p<\infty$, in terms of local BMO.
papers.title: Hardy and BMO spaces for the Laplacian with drift

papers.summary: We determine the even and odd derivations of the 91 entries in Gilg's classification list of complex filiform Lie superalgebras of superdimensions (2|2), (2|3), (2|4), (3|2), (3|3), (4|2), (5|2) and (6|2). A unified linear system yields explicit matrix parametrizations and the dimensions of both homogeneous components of the derivation superalgebra. The results are given in block-matrix form.
papers.title: Derivations of Low-Dimensional Filiform Lie Superalgebras

papers.summary: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of the continuation monad proposed to address the inefficiencies associated with the selection monad in alpha-beta search. We illustrate our approach with an implementation of Tic-Tac-Toe, observing a 39-fold reduction in the number of plays evaluated, compared with exhaustive search, in computing an optimal play. Finally, we formally establish the correctness of our construction by proving that the monadic alpha-beta search computes the same optimal outcomes and plays as exhaustive minimax search. Our results demonstrate how a foundational algorithm in AI can be expressed and verified using standard monadic abstractions, providing a basis for further development of compositional approaches to adversarial search.
papers.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations

papers.summary: Recall that $\mathsf{IOpen}$ denotes the theory of quantifier-free induction in the pure arithmetic language. In this paper, we consider an extension of $\mathsf{IOpen}$ in the arithmetical language expanded by the unary function $\exp: x \mapsto 2^x$, obtained by adding certain simple universal axioms for $\exp$, namely, $$\exp(1) = 2, \quad \exp(x + y) = \exp(x) \exp(y), \quad \exp(x) > x.$$ We prove that this theory is $Π_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{IOpen}$ and $\forall$-conservative over the theory of discretely ordered $\mathbb Z$-semirings. This result extends a result of A. Wilkie and provides a partial answer to a question of E. Jeřábek concerning the strength of the theory of exponential integer parts.
papers.title: Some conservativity results for weak arithmetic theories in a language with exponentiation

papers.summary: We construct a topos for Borel mathematics: statements which are true in Borel mathemaics correspond in a precise way to statements which are true in the internal logic of this topos. We investigate several other properties of this topos, including proving that it satisfies a Borel analogue of the Church-Turing thesis: the statement that every function on a standard Borel space is Borel. We also show that an earlier construction of a similar "Borel topos" by van Osdol does not suit these purposes because of an error in that paper.
papers.title: The Borel Topos
